newsitem.title: USA: Brown & Williamson firings illegal - lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Brown & Williamson firings illegal - lawyer.

text.p: A lawyer representing plaintiffs in a class-action lawsuit filed against Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp said Thursday that a federal judge has ruled the company violated labor laws by firing its sales force in 1995.

The lead class-action lawyer, Frederick Santarelli of Blue Bell, Pa., said the sales force of 1,000 workers was fired when the tobacco company and its parent, B.A.T Industries Plc acquired the American Tobacco Co in 1994, it said.

Santarelli, from the law firm of Elliot Reihner Siedzikowski & Egan, said the court ruled that the company violated federal labor laws by failing to give workers 60 days notice before terminating their jobs.
A class action lawsuit was filed by sales workers who were employed out of the company's Chester, Va., office.
The law firm said it anticipated damages would exceed $1 million.
Brown & Williamson, a unit of B.A.T Industries Plc, could be not reached immediately for comment.

In a statement released late on Thursday afternoon, Brown & Williamson contended the former American Tobacco employees were not covered under the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act "and were not disadvantaged in their salary continuation and benefits."
The company said all former American Tobacco workers had their salary and benefits extended for periods that depended on the number of years they were employed.
"The absolute minimum salary continuation was three months salary and benefits for each affected employee," it said.
For example, the two named plaintiffs in the case, Louis Ciarlante and Thomas Marshall, received salary and benefits for 48 weeks and 52 weeks, respectively.
The company said it is evaluating its options, including a possible request the trial court reconsider the ruling and an appeal of the decision.
